top_signals.title: Seven Months After Maduro's Fall, Big Oil Still Won't Commit To Venezuela
top_signals.summary: Venezuela's long-awaited oil revival has been slower than many in Washington anticipated, according to the Wall Street Journal. Seven months after Nicolás Maduro's removal, negotiations between the interim government and major U.S. energy companies remain bogged down, with no landmark investment deals despite the country's vast crude reserves. Rather than rushing back into the country, firms such as ExxonMobil and Chevron are taking a cautious approach. Executives remain wary of Venezuela's history of nationalizing foreign assets, unresolved…
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: Secular Bull Market Will Last Rest of Decade, Bartels Says
top_signals.summary: Mary Ann Bartels, Sanctuary Wealth chief investment strategist, says earnings should be celebrated and she says the secular bull market will go out until the end of the decade. She also says the Japanese yen has further to fall. She speaks on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)
top_signals.why_it_matters: Central-bank repricing affecting yields, FX, liquidity and equities.
